es: Diagnosticar y corregir errores de interacción profesional en cuatro áreas: registro, turnos, seguimiento y tacto.

vocabulary.es: hablar por encima de alguien, no dejarle terminar
suavizar el golpe de una mala noticia

teaching.en: In a first email to a senior manager, a formal register protects you from sounding overly familiar, however friendly your intentions are.
teaching.es: En un primer correo a un directivo, un registro formal evita que suenes demasiado familiar, por muy amistosas que sean tus intenciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Register = registro: la forma de pedir (Could you…? / I would be grateful if…) debe encajar con quien lee.
segments: In a first email to a senior manager, a formal register
protects you from sounding overly familiar, however friendly your intentions are.
teaching.audioText: In a first email to a senior manager, a formal register protects you from sounding overly familiar, however friendly your intentions are.

teaching.en: 'That will never work' is blunt, but 'I am not sure it will; could we test it first?' sounds tactful.
teaching.es: «Eso nunca funcionará» es brusco, pero «No estoy seguro de que lo haga; ¿podríamos probarlo primero?» suena diplomático.
teaching.explanationEs: Blunt = brusco, sin suavizar; tactful = con tacto. El contenido es el mismo: cambia cómo lo presentas.
segments: 'That will never work' is blunt, but 'I am not
sure it will; could we test it first?' sounds tactful.
teaching.audioText: 'That will never work' is blunt, but 'I am not sure it will; could we test it first?' sounds tactful.

teaching.en: Sorry to interrupt, but may I take the floor for a moment before we move on?
teaching.es: Perdona que interrumpa, pero ¿puedo tomar la palabra un momento antes de pasar al siguiente punto?
teaching.explanationEs: Sorry to + verbo pide paso con cortesía; take the floor = tomar la palabra. No se dice «sorry for interrupt».
segments: Sorry to interrupt, but may I take the
floor for a moment before we move on?
teaching.audioText: Sorry to interrupt, but may I take the floor for a moment before we move on?

teaching.en: If you talk over a colleague, you take away their turn, and the meeting soon feels like a contest.
teaching.es: Si hablas por encima de un colega, le quitas su turno, y la reunión pronto parece una competición.
teaching.explanationEs: Talk over = hablar a la vez que otro y anular su intervención; turn = turno de palabra.
segments: If you talk over a colleague, you take away their
turn, and the meeting soon feels like a contest.
teaching.audioText: If you talk over a colleague, you take away their turn, and the meeting soon feels like a contest.

teaching.en: To build rapport with a stranger, diagnose what they care about, then ask a follow-up question that shows genuine interest.
teaching.es: Para conectar con un desconocido, averigua qué le importa y hazle una pregunta de seguimiento que muestre un interés sincero.
teaching.explanationEs: Diagnose = identificar la causa. Una pregunta de seguimiento retoma las palabras del otro; una pregunta ajena corta la conversación.
segments: To build rapport with a stranger, diagnose what they care
about, then ask a follow-up question that shows genuine interest.
teaching.audioText: To build rapport with a stranger, diagnose what they care about, then ask a follow-up question that shows genuine interest.

teaching.en: Bad news is easier to hear when you soften the blow with a real strength, provided the message stays honest and tactful.
teaching.es: Una mala noticia se oye mejor si suavizas el golpe con un punto fuerte real, siempre que el mensaje siga siendo honesto y diplomático.
teaching.explanationEs: Soften the blow = suavizar el golpe: se suaviza la forma, no se oculta el hecho.
segments: Bad news is easier to hear when you soften the blow
with a real strength, provided the message stays honest and tactful.
teaching.audioText: Bad news is easier to hear when you soften the blow with a real strength, provided the message stays honest and tactful.

prompt.es: ¿Qué área falla en el correo que Tom envía a la clienta?

choices.text: Turns: Tom answers before the client has finished.
Follow-up: Tom ignores a question the client asked.
Tact: Tom complains about how slowly the client usually replies.
Register: the tone is too blunt for a senior client.

feedback.es: Tom da una orden seca a una clienta con la que no tiene confianza: es un fallo de registro. No hay intercambio oral ni crítica explícita a su lentitud.

hint.es: Fíjate en cómo pide algo Tom a alguien con autoridad sobre él.

origin.text: Tom writes to a client: Hi Mrs Okafor, send me the signed contract by Friday. I need it now because my boss is waiting. Thanks. Tom

prompt.es: Completa: «Perdona que interrumpa, pero ¿puedo tomar la palabra un momento?»

feedback.es: Sorry to + verbo es la fórmula cortés para pedir paso; interrupt es el verbo que exige el espacio en blanco, no una forma con for.

hint.es: Después de sorry, la acción inmediata lleva to + verbo base.

origin.text: Dr Lee was halfway through her explanation when Tom cut in with a question. She stopped, clearly annoyed. Tom could have said: Sorry to ___, but may I take the floor for a moment?

prompt.es: Ordena: «Déjame terminar este punto y luego será tu turno.»

answer.text: Let me finish this point and then it will be your turn
accepted: Let me finish this point and then it will be your turn
Let me finish this point and then it is your turn

feedback.es: Let me + verbo base reclama el turno sin agresividad, y la segunda parte promete dar la palabra al otro.

hint.es: Empieza por la fórmula que pide permiso para terminar.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué muestra la reacción de Sara en la reunión.

choices.text: She hands the turn to Carlos so that the room can relax.
She politely tells Carlos that his own figures are wrong.
She keeps her turn firmly but without attacking him.

feedback.es: Sara reclama su turno con calma («Let me finish this point») y promete cederlo después. No se lo entrega a Carlos ni le dice que sus cifras estén mal: es Carlos quien sostiene que las de ella lo están.

origin.audio: During the budget meeting, Sara was explaining her figures when Carlos began to talk over her, insisting that the numbers were wrong. Sara lowered her voice and said: Let me finish this point, and then it is your turn. Carlos sat back, and the room relaxed.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con lo que hace el hablante en la conversación.

pairs.es: Anula el turno de otro sin dejarle terminar
Pide la palabra para intervenir
Comunica algo desagradable con delicadeza
Crea una buena relación con alguien

feedback.es: Cada expresión describe un movimiento distinto de la conversación: anular un turno, pedirlo, suavizar una mala noticia y conectar.

pairs.es: Anula el turno de otro sin dejarle terminar
Pide la palabra para intervenir
Comunica algo desagradable con delicadeza
Crea una buena relación con alguien

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta de Leo muestra un interés sincero por lo que contó Ana?

choices.text: What is the hardest part of feeding so many patients?
Quito is lovely; I went once for a conference and it rained.
That must be tiring, and kitchens never pay very well.

feedback.es: La pregunta retoma el trabajo de Ana y pide más información: es seguimiento sincero. Hablar de su propio viaje desvía el tema y suponer que pagan mal es poco tacto.

origin.text: Ana: I have just moved from Quito to work in a hospital kitchen, and the shifts start at five in the morning.

prompt.es: ¿Qué corrección arregla el tacto de este borrador sin ocultar los hechos?

choices.text: We are very sorry that the report was late, and we accept full responsibility for the whole delay.
We sent the report on Monday; I have attached it again in case it was missed.
You should read your messages more carefully before telling us that a report is late.

feedback.es: Enviar el informe el lunes es un hecho que se mantiene, y se suaviza la forma. Aceptar toda la responsabilidad admite una culpa que no existe, y reprochar al cliente que no lea sus mensajes sigue siendo brusco.

origin.text: Draft reply to a client: Dear Ms Okafor, you said the report was late, but that is not true. We sent it on Monday, and you simply did not open it. Anyway, what time suits you for the call? Regards, Tom

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la reacción final de la directiva.

choices.text: She is eager to read the samples as soon as they arrive.
She thinks the samples are not needed because Leo has described his work.
She is polite, but she is not keen to continue the conversation.

feedback.es: «She would look out for them» es una fórmula cortés y vaga; junto con el vistazo al reloj y el saludo al siguiente invitado sugiere poco interés. Leo no mostró interés por ella.

origin.audio: At a business event, a manager mentioned that her team was looking for new people. Leo nodded, said it sounded very interesting, and then spent five minutes describing his own projects without asking her a single question. When she glanced at her watch, he added that he would send her some samples of his work. She smiled politely and said that she would look out for them. Then she turned to greet the next guest warmly.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para suavizar el golpe, primero elogió sus resultados.»

feedback.es: Soften the blow es la colocación habitual para dar una mala noticia con delicadeza; cushion y ease the blow también son naturales.

origin.text: The manager had to tell Sara that her promotion was postponed. To ___ the blow, he first praised her latest results and then explained the budget problem honestly.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Podríamos pasar la reunión al jueves, si te parece bien?»

answer.text: Could we move the meeting to Thursday if that suits you

feedback.es: Could we… propone sin imponer y if that suits you deja la decisión final al otro: es un registro cortés y flexible.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la directora sobre la propuesta de Leo?

choices.text: That it is unlikely to be accepted this time.
That it is interesting enough to be tested this year.
That the marketing team will now reconsider its campaign.
That Leo should have spoken to the marketing team before proposing it.

feedback.es: Agradecer, recordar que la campaña ya está reservada y aplazar la idea «para el próximo año» es una negativa cortés. La directora no dice que Leo debiera haber consultado antes.

origin.text: Leo proposed moving the launch to June. The director thanked him for the suggestion, noted that the marketing team had already booked its campaign, and added that it was 'an interesting idea for next year'.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué Ana deja de sonreír.

choices.text: Leo interrupted her before she had finished explaining.
Leo showed no interest in what she had just shared.
Leo made a joke about her sister and about Lima.

feedback.es: Ana comparte algo personal y Leo cambia de tema sin una pregunta de seguimiento: falta interés sincero. No la interrumpe ni bromea.

origin.audio: Ana told her new colleague that she had moved to Lima the previous year to join her sister. Leo replied that it sounded nice and immediately asked what time lunch was. Ana stopped smiling and turned back to her screen.

prompt.es: Completa: «La gente suele tomar la palabra solo cuando el moderador asiente.»

feedback.es: Take the floor es la colocación fija para tomar la palabra en una reunión; el verbo take es el que exige la expresión.

origin.text: After the presentation, the speaker invited questions. Sara raised her hand and waited, because in this company people usually ___ the floor only after the chair has nodded.

es: Repasar con precisión cuatro recursos formales: condicionales sin if, pasivas de reporte, nominalizaciones y lenguaje de proyección.

vocabulary.es: alegando que, con el argumento de que

teaching.en: In the event of a delay, and should you require further details, please contact the office.
teaching.es: En caso de retraso, y si necesita más detalles, póngase en contacto con la oficina.
teaching.explanationEs: Should + sujeto + verbo base sustituye a «if you should»: posibilidad futura, registro formal. In the event of + nombre = en caso de.
segments: In the event of a delay, and should
you require further details, please contact the office.
teaching.audioText: In the event of a delay, and should you require further details, please contact the office.

teaching.en: Had we known about the delay earlier, we would have drawn up a contingency plan.
teaching.es: De haber sabido del retraso antes, habríamos elaborado un plan de contingencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Had + sujeto + participio sustituye a «if we had known»: pasado irreal y formal.
segments: Had we known about the delay earlier, we
would have drawn up a contingency plan.
teaching.audioText: Had we known about the delay earlier, we would have drawn up a contingency plan.

teaching.en: Were the council to approve the budget, work would begin in May, although nothing has been decided yet.
teaching.es: Si el ayuntamiento aprobara el presupuesto, las obras empezarían en mayo, aunque todavía no se ha decidido nada.
teaching.explanationEs: Were + sujeto + to + verbo plantea una hipótesis remota, sin if.
segments: Were the council to approve the budget, work would
begin in May, although nothing has been decided yet.
teaching.audioText: Were the council to approve the budget, work would begin in May, although nothing has been decided yet.

teaching.en: The minister is reported to have resigned last night, although no official statement has been made.
teaching.es: Se informa de que el ministro dimitió anoche, aunque no se ha hecho ninguna declaración oficial.
teaching.explanationEs: Is reported to have + participio: el hecho es anterior y la fuente queda general.
segments: The minister is reported to have resigned last
night, although no official statement has been made.
teaching.audioText: The minister is reported to have resigned last night, although no official statement has been made.

teaching.en: A sharp increase in fares led to a steep fall in passenger numbers and a serious shortfall in income.
teaching.es: Un fuerte aumento de las tarifas provocó una caída brusca del número de pasajeros y un grave déficit de ingresos.
teaching.explanationEs: Nominalización: increase, fall y shortfall son nombres y van con in, no con of. Sharp y steep son los adjetivos de grado.
segments: A sharp increase in fares led to a steep fall
in passenger numbers and a serious shortfall in income.
teaching.audioText: A sharp increase in fares led to a steep fall in passenger numbers and a serious shortfall in income.

teaching.en: Sales are projected to double by 2030, and the firm is set to open ten stores on the grounds that demand will keep growing.
teaching.es: Se prevé que las ventas se dupliquen para 2030 y la empresa tiene previsto abrir diez tiendas, con el argumento de que la demanda seguirá creciendo.
teaching.explanationEs: Projected to / set to + verbo: proyección apoyada en datos o planes. On the grounds that introduce la razón que se alega.
segments: Sales are projected to double by 2030, and the firm is set
to open ten stores on the grounds that demand will keep growing.
teaching.audioText: Sales are projected to double by 2030, and the firm is set to open ten stores on the grounds that demand will keep growing.

prompt.es: Completa, sin if: «Si necesita una sala más grande, avise en recepción.»

feedback.es: Para una posibilidad futura en registro formal se abre con Should y se omite if; el resto de la frase sigue igual.

hint.es: Empieza el aviso formal sin if: auxiliar + sujeto + verbo base.

origin.text: The library is changing its opening hours next month. A notice on the door reads: ___ you require a larger study room, please tell the front desk at least a day in advance.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase recoge que el puente cerró en junio, según varias fuentes?

choices.text: The bridge is reported to close to traffic in June.
The bridge is reporting to have closed to traffic in June.
The bridge is reported to have closed to traffic in June.

feedback.es: El cierre es anterior al momento en que se informa, así que se necesita to have + participio; con el infinitivo simple se hablaría de un hecho futuro o habitual.

hint.es: El cierre ya ocurrió: necesitas to have + participio.

origin.text: Several news agencies say that the bridge closed to traffic in June after cracks were found, but the council has not commented yet.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un fuerte aumento de las tarifas provocó una caída brusca.»

answer.text: A sharp increase in fares led to a steep fall

feedback.es: Increase y fall son nombres y se unen a lo que cambia con in; sharp y steep gradúan el tamaño del cambio.

hint.es: El sujeto es un nombre con adjetivo: sharp increase in fares.

prompt.es: Ordena: «De haberlo sabido antes, habríamos cambiado de hotel.»

answer.text: Had we known earlier we would have changed hotels
accepted: Had we known earlier we would have changed hotels
We would have changed hotels had we known earlier

feedback.es: Had + sujeto + participio abre la frase formal y la consecuencia lleva would have + participio; el orden inverso también es correcto.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo presenta el hablante el cierre de la biblioteca.

choices.text: As a hypothetical scenario that nobody has proposed.
As a plan that the head teacher is reluctant to confirm.
As a rumour that parents have decided to ignore.

feedback.es: Were … to plantea una hipótesis remota y la directora niega que exista el plan. Los padres no ignoran el rumor: les preocupa y dicen que protestarían.

origin.audio: Were the school to close the library, students would have nowhere quiet to study. The head teacher insists that no such plan exists, but the rumour has already upset many parents, who say they would complain loudly if it were ever proposed.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada estructura con el grado de realidad que expresa.

pairs: Were the firm to lose the contract

pairs.es: Hipótesis remota: no se espera que ocurra
Posibilidad futura, en registro formal
Plan ya decidido para el futuro
Hecho pasado atribuido a otras fuentes

feedback.es: Cada estructura marca un grado distinto de realidad: hipótesis remota, posibilidad, plan decidido y hecho pasado atribuido.

pairs: Were the firm to lose the contract

pairs.es: Hipótesis remota: no se espera que ocurra
Posibilidad futura, en registro formal
Plan ya decidido para el futuro
Hecho pasado atribuido a otras fuentes

prompt.es: Completa las tres frases formales: proyección, nominalización y condicional.

feedback.es: Projected to introduce una previsión, steep fall va con in y Were … to plantea la hipótesis remota sin if.

sentences: Profits are ___ to rise by four per cent next year.
A steep fall ___ demand could make the firm delay the plan.
___ the firm to lose the contract, it would have to close a workshop.
origin.text: Extract from a company report: the firm is planning a major expansion, and its owners have been warned about several risks.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugieren los vecinos sobre el ayuntamiento.

choices.text: That the council has already proved the owners are guilty.
That earlier checks could have reduced the harm.
That the council will publish the final findings itself.

feedback.es: La frase con Had the council inspected… es un pasado irreal que atribuyen los vecinos: con inspecciones anteriores el daño habría sido menor. Quien publicará sus conclusiones es la empresa, no el ayuntamiento.

origin.audio: According to several reports, the plant is thought to have put waste into the river for years, although its owners have denied any fault. Had the council inspected the site earlier, residents say, the damage would have been far smaller. Fish have disappeared from the lower stretch, and some families have stopped using the water. A full investigation is due to start next month, and the company is set to publish its own findings shortly afterwards.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión corrige los dos errores de este aviso?

choices.text: Had we known about the strike, we would have warned everyone. The increase of ticket prices is said to have upset many commuters.
Had we know about the strike, we would have warned everyone. The increase in ticket prices is said to have upset many commuters.
Had we known about the strike, we would have warned everyone. The increase in ticket prices is said to have upset many commuters.

feedback.es: Hay que corregir ambas cosas: después de Had + sujeto va el participio known y el aumento de precios se construye con in. Las otras versiones dejan un error.

origin.text: Mia drafted a notice for passengers: 'Had we knew about the strike, we would have warned everyone. The increase of ticket prices is said to have upset many commuters.'

prompt.es: Redacta en inglés formal dos frases: una previsión y un aviso con Should.

answer.text: Sales are projected to rise by five per cent next year. Should there be a delay, the company will inform its clients.
accepted: Sales are projected to rise by five per cent next year. Should there be a delay, the company will inform its clients.
Sales are expected to increase by five per cent next year. Should a delay occur, the company will notify its clients.
Sales are forecast to grow by 5 per cent next year. Should there be any delay, the company will contact its customers.

feedback.es: Una previsión se formula con projected/expected to + verbo, y el aviso formal abre con Should + sujeto + verbo base, sin if.

origin.text: Dos frases formales para un informe: 1) se prevé que las ventas suban un cinco por ciento el año próximo (is projected to); 2) si hubiera un retraso, la empresa avisaría a sus clientes (Should, sin if).

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión nominalizada condensa mejor el informe?

choices.text: A ten per cent rise in parking fees led to a fall in the number of drivers and a loss of income.
A ten per cent rise of parking fees led to a fall of the number of drivers and a loss of income.
A ten per cent rise in parking fees led to a fall on the number of drivers and a loss on income.

feedback.es: Con rise, fall y loss la preposición que señala lo que cambia es in (o of para loss of income). Las otras versiones calcan el español con of o usan una preposición incorrecta.

origin.text: Report: The council raised parking fees by ten per cent, so fewer drivers came into the town centre, and the shopkeepers there lost income as a result.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ocurrió en realidad con el horario del ferri.

choices.text: The timetable came out early, but the ferry still left late.
The timetable came out late and passengers were stranded.
The passengers were stranded although the timetable was ready.

feedback.es: Had … published es pasado irreal: la empresa no lo publicó antes, y por eso los pasajeros quedaron varados. Las otras opciones invierten la situación.

origin.audio: Had the ferry company published its timetable earlier, hundreds of passengers would not have been stranded at the port. As it is, the delay is reported to have lasted nine hours, and the company is set to offer compensation, provided that passengers submit a claim within thirty days.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los vecinos notaron un fuerte aumento del ruido.»

feedback.es: Sharp increase in es la colocación natural para un cambio brusco; la preposición in señala qué aumenta.

origin.text: Residents noticed a sharp ___ in noise after the new road opened. A steep rise in traffic is said to be the cause, and the council is set to measure the levels next week.

es: Analizar el tono, la postura y las implicaciones de un fragmento de pódcast o de una canción, citando la pista que lo demuestra.

vocabulary.es: al pie de la letra, tal cual

teaching.en: Taken at face value, the host's praise sounds sincere, yet the word supposedly quietly hints at doubt.
teaching.es: Tomado al pie de la letra, el elogio de la presentadora suena sincero, pero la palabra «supuestamente» insinúa duda con discreción.
teaching.explanationEs: At face value = tal cual se dice. Supposedly pone distancia: el hablante no se compromete con que sea verdad.
segments: Taken at face value, the host's praise sounds sincere,
yet the word supposedly quietly hints at doubt.
teaching.audioText: Taken at face value, the host's praise sounds sincere, yet the word supposedly quietly hints at doubt.

teaching.en: A single word can set the tone: when the host says supposedly, she keeps her distance and sounds sceptical.
teaching.es: Una sola palabra puede marcar el tono: cuando la presentadora dice «supuestamente», se distancia y suena escéptica.
teaching.explanationEs: Set the tone = marcar el tono. Sceptical = escéptico: duda de lo que dice otro.
segments: A single word can set the tone: when the host
says supposedly, she keeps her distance and sounds sceptical.
teaching.audioText: A single word can set the tone: when the host says supposedly, she keeps her distance and sounds sceptical.

teaching.en: In the second verse the singer sounds wistful, and the ironic undertone of the chorus suggests a smile that hides some pain.
teaching.es: En la segunda estrofa la cantante suena nostálgica, y el matiz irónico del estribillo sugiere una sonrisa que oculta algo de dolor.
teaching.explanationEs: Wistful = añoranza suave. Un undertone es lo que se percibe debajo de las palabras, sin decirlo.
segments: In the second verse the singer sounds wistful, and the ironic
undertone of the chorus suggests a smile that hides some pain.
teaching.audioText: In the second verse the singer sounds wistful, and the ironic undertone of the chorus suggests a smile that hides some pain.

teaching.en: Saying that a film is hardly a masterpiece may imply that it is weak, although the critic never uses that word.
teaching.es: Decir que una película no es precisamente una obra maestra puede dar a entender que es floja, aunque el crítico nunca use esa palabra.
teaching.explanationEs: Imply = dar a entender: la idea no se dice, se deduce. Hardly resta valor a la palabra siguiente.
segments: Saying that a film is hardly a masterpiece may imply that
it is weak, although the critic never uses that word.
teaching.audioText: Saying that a film is hardly a masterpiece may imply that it is weak, although the critic never uses that word.

teaching.en: What a guest leaves out can speak volumes, so a dismissive change of subject is itself a kind of answer.
teaching.es: Lo que un invitado omite puede decirlo todo, así que un cambio de tema despectivo ya es una forma de respuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Speak volumes = ser muy elocuente sin palabras. Dismissive = rechaza sin argumentar.
segments: What a guest leaves out can speak volumes, so a
dismissive change of subject is itself a kind of answer.
teaching.audioText: What a guest leaves out can speak volumes, so a dismissive change of subject is itself a kind of answer.

teaching.en: A host who refuses to take a stance may still reveal one through what she stresses and what she leaves out.
teaching.es: Una presentadora que se niega a adoptar una postura aún puede revelarla por lo que destaca y por lo que deja fuera.
teaching.explanationEs: Take a stance = adoptar una postura: la opinión ante el tema. Se infiere del énfasis y de las omisiones.
segments: A host who refuses to take a stance may still reveal
one through what she stresses and what she leaves out.
teaching.audioText: A host who refuses to take a stance may still reveal one through what she stresses and what she leaves out.

prompt.es: ¿Qué tono transmite la presentadora con la palabra supposedly?

choices.text: Sceptical: she keeps her distance from the council's promise.
Wistful: she misses the old bus route.
Dismissive: she thinks the plan is not worth discussing.

feedback.es: Supposedly y «we shall see» señalan duda ante la promesa del ayuntamiento, pero la presentadora sí trata el plan y no añora nada.

hint.es: Supposedly pone distancia: ¿se cree la presentadora lo que dice el ayuntamiento?

origin.text: Podcast host: The council says the new bus lane will supposedly cut delays by half. Residents have been waiting eight years for it, and, well, we shall see how that goes.

prompt.es: Completa: «En la segunda estrofa, el tono de la cantante es nostálgico.»

feedback.es: Wistful describe una añoranza suave, por eso encaja con quien recuerda una calle desaparecida con una sonrisa triste.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo para el tono de quien recuerda el pasado con suave tristeza.

origin.text: The singer remembers a street that no longer exists, and she smiles sadly as she does so. In the second verse, her tone is ___.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la crítica sin decirlo directamente?

choices.text: That the film is excellent but rather too long.
That the film is weak overall, despite a few good details.
That the film failed only because of its costumes.

prompt.es: Escribe tu historia de 220 a 270 palabras con gancho, tensión, giro, énfasis y reflexión.

answer.text: I still remember the night I missed the last train. I was a student, and I had spent the whole evening at a friend's birthday party in the next town. When I reached the station, the platform was empty and the clock showed midnight. My phone had no battery, and the nearest taxi was far away. I sat on a cold bench and tried to stay calm. It was not the dark that frightened me; it was the silence. Never had I heard a city so quiet. Then, behind me, I heard footsteps. They were slow, and they were coming closer. I held my bag tightly and did not look back. 'Are you waiting for the last train?' a voice asked. I looked up, and my heart stopped. The man in front of me was wearing a long grey coat, and he looked strangely familiar. He turned out to be Mr Duarte, my new science teacher, who lived two streets away. He smiled, offered me a lift and even gave me his phone charger. All the way home I kept thinking about how afraid I had been of a person who only wanted to help. Looking back, I realise that the real problem was not the empty station. It was my habit of expecting the worst and of staying silent when I needed help. Since that night, I ask for help earlier, and I listen for the kind voice before I imagine the dangerous one.

Looking back, I realise that the real problem was not the empty station. It was my habit of expecting the worst and of staying silent when I needed help. Since that night, I ask for help earlier, and I listen for the kind voice before I imagine the dangerous one.

The night I missed the last train began like any other. I was at a party in the next town, and I left too late. On the platform, the clock showed midnight and nobody was there. I sat down and waited, because my phone had no battery. What frightened me most was the silence. Then I heard footsteps behind me, slow and close. I did not dare to look. The lights were weak, and the wind moved some old paper along the ground. A voice said, 'Are you waiting for the last train?' I looked up, and there was my new science teacher, Mr Duarte, in a long grey coat. It turned out that he lived nearby, and he offered me a lift home. In the car we hardly spoke, but it was warm, and the radio played softly. I felt almost ashamed. I had been afraid of a man who only wanted to help. Looking back, I learned that I often expect the worst when I am alone. Never again will I stay silent when I need help.

prompt.es: Escribe al casero: preséntate, negocia con condiciones y repara un malentendido.

answer.text: Dear Mr Reid, Good morning. I am a newcomer to the city, and I am writing about the flat on Elm Street. I arrived last week, and I am looking for a quiet place near my new job. I have seen the photographs, and I would like to visit the flat this week if that is possible. I work as a translator, so I am at home during the day and I will look after the flat carefully. I can pay the deposit now, provided that the rent is 650 a month instead of 700. In exchange for the lower rent, I would sign a twelve-month contract, and I could start on the first of next month. I think that would be a fair compromise for both of us, and I am sure we can reach an agreement that suits you. I also think there was a misunderstanding about the floor: I meant the second floor, not the first. Let me clarify this now so that we can avoid any problem later. Thank you very much for your patience, and I look forward to your reply. Kind regards, Carlos

Dear Mr Reid, I have just arrived in the city, so I am new to everything. I am interested in the flat on Elm Street, and I would like to visit it this week. I would pay the deposit today as long as the rent is 650 a month and not 700. In return, I can offer a twelve-month contract, and I can move in at the start of next month. I believe that would be a fair compromise. I also think there was a mix-up about the floor, because what I meant was the second floor. I would like to clarify this before we meet so that nobody is disappointed. Thank you for your time and your patience. Yours sincerely, Carlos

feedback.es: Un mensaje completo se presenta como recién llegado, ofrece con condición (provided that), propone un intercambio, repara sin culpar y cierra con cortesía.

origin.text: Acabas de llegar a una ciudad nueva. Escribe al casero, el señor Reid: preséntate como recién llegado; ofrece pagar la fianza ahora si el alquiler baja de 700 a 650; ofrece un contrato de doce meses a cambio; propón un compromiso justo; repara un malentendido: querías decir la segunda planta, no la primera; cierra con cortesía.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué revela la condición del casero sobre sus prioridades.

choices.text: He hopes she will refuse so that he can raise the rent.
He is mainly worried that the bills will not be paid.
He would rather have a stable tenant than a higher rent.

feedback.es: Acepta incluir las facturas a cambio de un año de contrato: prefiere estabilidad a un alquiler mayor. No rechaza nada ni menciona impagos.

origin.audio: The tenant said she would take the flat if the bills were included in the rent. The landlord replied that he could do that, but only if she signed for a year. She thought for a moment, asked whether the contract could be ended early in an emergency, and then agreed when he said that it could, provided that she gave two months' notice. He wrote the figures down carefully, and they agreed to meet on Monday.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión corrige el registro sin perder lo que se quiere pedir?

choices.text: Good morning, Mr Reid. Would it be possible to move the viewing to another day? I would also like to discuss the rent.
Good morning, Mr Reid. I am afraid you will have to change the viewing, and the rent must go down.
Dear Mr Reid, I am so sorry to trouble you, but I cannot possibly come, and I will not mention the rent.

feedback.es: Mantiene las dos peticiones (cambiar la visita y hablar del alquiler) con fórmulas corteses. La segunda sigue siendo una orden y la tercera se disculpa tanto que renuncia a pedir.

origin.text: Message to the landlord: Hey. I can't come on Thursday, so change the viewing. And the rent you said is too high, fix it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lograron cerrar un trato antes de que terminara la visita.»

feedback.es: Strike a deal es la colocación habitual para cerrar un acuerdo tras negociar; reach y make a deal también son naturales.

origin.text: After an hour of talks, the landlord lowered the rent and Carlos accepted a longer contract. It was not the price either of them wanted, but they managed to ___ a deal before the viewing ended.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué este modo de reparar el malentendido funciona.

choices.text: She shows that the agent made the mistake in the first place.
She accepts her share of the confusion and offers a practical solution.
She postpones the meeting until the agent has calmed down.

feedback.es: Reconoce su parte, repite el día correcto y ofrece una solución: repara sin culpar. No acusa al agente de oír mal ni aplaza nada.

origin.audio: Ana had told the agent that the keys would be ready on Friday. When he phoned on Friday morning, she realised that she had meant Thursday. Instead of defending herself, she apologised for the confusion, repeated the correct day, and offered to collect the keys herself that afternoon.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el casero con su última frase?

choices.text: That the landlord has already refused Carlos's offer.
That Carlos should decide quickly or risk losing the flat.
That twelve months is too long a contract for the landlord.
That the other visitors have offered a higher rent.

feedback.es: La mención de otras visitas y de un plazo hasta el viernes presiona con cortesía: decide pronto o podrías perder el departamento. No rechaza la oferta ni dice nada de otros alquileres.

origin.text: Dear Carlos, thank you for your offer. Twelve months is certainly something we can discuss, and I appreciate your quick reply. However, several other people have already visited the flat this week, so I would be grateful for a decision by Friday.

prompt.es: Propón un trato: «Acepto el contrato, siempre que el alquiler sea de 650.»

answer.text: I accept the contract provided that the rent is 650.
accepted: I accept the contract provided that the rent is 650.
I will accept the contract providing that the rent is 650.
I accept the contract as long as the rent is 650.

feedback.es: Provided that (o as long as) presenta la condición de tu aceptación, y el alquiler queda fijado en el presente simple.

origin.text: Acepto el contrato, siempre que el alquiler sea de 650.
